items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: Nat Hentoff and Martin Williams and a guy named Hsio Wen Shih, a Chinese man, started a magazine called the Jazz Review. It only lasted a couple of years. But their idea was to get musicians to write reviews.

ctx.x: Well that’s great. That’s some major scuffling. When did you first start to do some writing?

Well I had done writing just as a writing exercise all through school and college. One of the best college courses I ever took was a creative writing class where the woman gave us a lot of freedom, just showed us how to research and gave us a lot of freedom to write whatever we wanted. And somewhere I think after I started working for Stan Getz in about 1953, in there someplace, I had been through let’s see, Teddy Charles I think was my first really jazz group. I worked with his trio and he taught me all the…
professional writer and I’m not going to get in anybody’s way by saying what I think about some things that I review there, but I don’t really like reviewing music anymore.
